ASVA does not operate an ambulance, does not control traffic directly, and does not replace clinical judgment. It coordinates information, routing, live movement visibility, and secure pre-arrival handoff.

ASVA is a premium emergency medical coordination web platform connecting the ambulance journey, receiving hospital, and authorized traffic-control operations in real time. It targets road accidents, fire incidents, flood/disaster response, and home-originated medical emergencies.

Core loop: the app opens on a plain live map for the ambulance en route to the patient. Once the crew physically reaches the patient, the operator taps Patient Found, which triggers a nearest-hospital search showing five candidates (government and private). The operator selects a hospital, the app returns the route and ETA, and the app then prompts for the minimum necessary patient data via voice, quick-select, or manual entry. Transport data (registration, location, destination, ETA) is captured and sent automatically, with no manual step. The helper verifies clinical data before it is sent; the hospital receives a pre-arrival snapshot and live updates, and on arrival can continue the record and issue a secure referral handoff.
ASVA helps an emergency patient reach the appropriate hospital through the best available route while the patient's verified information and ambulance movement travel ahead of the patient.
MVP feature tiering (P0/P1/P2/P3) so the build order is unambiguous under time pressure.

Eight additional feature modules that raise competitiveness: multi-hospital broadcast/accept, bed and resource capacity board, ambulance-to-ambulance mutual aid, ETA-aware traffic pre-clearance requests, offline-first PWA mode, family/next-of-kin notification link, AI triage-priority scoring, and analytics/command dashboard.

Hospital selection happens immediately after patient contact, before the detailed data form, so the route to definitive care starts as early as possible. Data capture happens during transit, not before dispatch, so it never delays getting the ambulance moving.
Receiving hospitals often know nothing about an incoming patient until the ambulance arrives, losing preparation time.
Typing a long clinical form inside a moving ambulance is slow, distracting, and often unsafe for the helper.
Critical information captured verbally or on paper must be repeated at the hospital, introducing delay and transcription error.
Traffic-control teams lack a unified, real-time view of emergency ambulance routes and movement.
Inter-hospital referrals require repeated manual communication, delaying access to treatment history and reports.
During mass-casualty or disaster events, there is no shared view of which hospitals have capacity, so ambulances can converge on already-saturated ERs.
Families of patients are frequently left without timely, verified updates during transport.
Route the ambulance to the most appropriate hospital using the best available path.

ASVA is not an ambulance operator or fleet-management company.
ASVA does not directly control traffic signals; the traffic-control interface only provides authorized operational information for human or approved systems to act on.
ASVA does not make final diagnosis or treatment decisions; all scoring and AI extraction are assistive and must be verified before becoming an official clinical record.
ASVA does not block emergency movement because optional profile details are missing.
ASVA does not replace a hospital's internal EHR/EMR system; it hands off a structured summary and documents, not a full medical record migration.

16.2 Suggested stack (aligned to your existing toolkit)
Frontend: React (Vite) or Next.js, Tailwind for the glass design system, deployed responsive-first.

Backend/data: Firebase (Firestore + Realtime DB for live tracking + Auth), matching prior experience, or a lightweight Node/Express + Postgres API if relational modeling is preferred for the audit log and referral tokens.
Maps/routing: Google Maps Platform (Directions + Places) or Mapbox.
Speech-to-text: Web Speech API for a fast demo path, or a cloud STT API (Google/Whisper) for accuracy.
QR: client-side QR generator + server-issued signed/opaque token (JWT with short expiry + revocation list, or a random token mapped server-side).
Hosting: Vercel/Netlify for frontend, Firebase Functions or a small Node server for backend logic.
Ambulance client writes case + patient data to Case/Patient services, tagged with verification state.
On journey start, Location service begins streaming GPS at a fixed interval (e.g. every 3-5s) to a Firestore/WebSocket channel scoped to that case.
Traffic dashboard and Hospital dashboard subscribe to the same case channel with role-scoped field visibility (traffic never receives clinical fields).
Voice input goes through the Voice/NLP service, returns a structured diff, which is merged into the patient record only after helper confirmation.
Hospital-matching service re-ranks candidate hospitals whenever bed/resource data or ETA changes meaningfully, without disrupting an already-accepted case.
Referral flow creates an immutable referral package with a QR-encoded opaque token; scanning resolves via an authenticated server call, never by decoding data directly from the QR.

23. Build Principles for the Development Team
Build the product as a responsive web platform with desktop-first dashboards and tablet-friendly emergency workflows.
Keep ambulance data entry extremely fast and touch-friendly.
Keep the patient review/verification step explicit; never auto-submit.
Use one shared design system across all dashboards while adapting density and controls to each role.
Keep live location, routing, and patient data services logically separated so one failure does not collapse the whole emergency workflow.
Design all critical workflows for graceful degradation and transparent sync state.
Prioritize reliability, auditability, and clear user status over decorative animation.
Build P0 completely and demo-stable before touching P1; a working narrow loop beats a broad broken one.
24. Build Brief for an AI Code Generator

Build ASVA as a responsive, desktop-first emergency medical coordination web platform using the ASVA logo and an iOS 26-inspired Liquid Glass visual system. Create role-based experiences for Ambulance, Hospital Admin/ER, Traffic Control, and System Admin.

The app opens on a plain live Google Map while the ambulance travels to the patient; no hospital list or patient form is shown at this stage. On arrival at the scene, the operator taps a single prominent Patient Found button, which immediately triggers a nearest-hospital search returning 5 candidates (a mix of government and private, ranked by distance/ETA). The operator selects one hospital, and the app instantly returns the route and live ETA.

Only after hospital selection does the app prompt the minimum-necessary-data workflow: patient basics (age, sex, blood type), emergency context, current condition including GCS and pupil assessment where relevant, vital signs, critical medical information (allergies, key disease, blood thinners), and treatment already given. Support voice-to-structured-data, quick-select, radio buttons, and manual editing, and require helper verification before this clinical data is sent. Separately, transport data (ambulance registration, current location, destination hospital, ETA) must be captured and sent automatically the moment a hospital is selected, with no manual step, and should also stream continuously to the authorized traffic-control dashboard.

On the hospital side, show a compact doctor-facing summary card first (case ID, sex, approximate age, emergency type, ETA, GCS, BP, HR, SpO2, RR, major injury, allergy, important medication, treatment given), with up/down arrows flagging abnormal values, before the doctor opens the full record.

Build the P1 differentiators once the core loop is stable: multi-hospital broadcast with first-accept routing, a bed/resource capacity board feeding hospital ranking, an AI-assisted (clearly labeled, non-diagnostic) triage-priority score sorting the hospital's incoming queue, and a secure QR-based hospital-to-hospital referral handoff.

The hospital dashboard must show incoming patient cards, live updates, trends, and timeline. Keep traffic users limited to operational ambulance information and never expose clinical data. Make critical information highly legible even within the glass UI. Do not turn ASVA into an ambulance service or a treatment-decision engine.
